user.title: Kohler Anthem Plus
user.description: Sign in with your Kohler Konnect account. Sign-in happens entirely within Home Assistant — there is no browser step and nothing to copy back.

valve.title: Select your valve
valve.description:
Found: {summary}

Your valve's outlet layout could not be read automatically, so choose your Anthem digital valve model. This decides how many outlets exist and which zone each belongs to. It is required even with only an Anthem Plus controller, because the controller reports outlets per zone using the same layout.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The saved session for {username} has expired. Enter the password again to reconnect.

error.invalid_auth: Kohler rejected that email or password.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Kohler. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.signin_blocked: Kohler needs an extra step to sign in (for example two-factor authentication), which this integration cannot complete.
error.no_devices: That account has no Anthem or Anthem Plus devices. Note that an Anthem Plus touchscreen (K-28214-ASC) only adds the controller — adding the valve itself requires a first-generation Anthem touchscreen (K-28214).

abort.already_configured: This Kohler account is already set up.

endless_shower_not_set_up.title: Endless Shower is waiting on your valve
endless_shower_not_set_up.description:
Endless Shower is turned on, but Home Assistant has not been able to read the shower time limit from your valve yet, so it cannot restart your shower.

**No action is needed.** The limit is normally read during setup, and Endless Shower arms itself the moment it arrives. This message clears on its own.

If it is still here after a few minutes, the valve is unreachable — check that it is online in the Kohler Konnect app, then reload the integration.

old_capture_folder.title: Old debug captures can be deleted

confirm.title: Delete the old capture folder?
confirm.description:
Versions before 0.4.1 wrote debug captures to `{path}` on every install — the author's own development tooling, switched on by mistake for everyone. Here it holds {count} files, {size_mb} MB. Nothing reads or writes them any more.

**Submit** deletes the folder. Choose **Ignore** on the issue to keep it instead — the files are inert either way.

This is separate from the Report Log switch, whose files live inside the integration folder and are not touched.

abort.not_ours: `{path}` holds something this integration did not write, so nothing was deleted. Remove the folder by hand if you no longer need it.
abort.failed: Deleting `{path}` did not go through. The folder is back at that path, possibly with fewer of the capture files than before. Home Assistant's log says why. Remove it by hand if you no longer need it.
abort.stranded: Deleting `{path}` stopped part-way and the folder could not be put back. Whatever is left is now at `{aside}`; remove it by hand. Home Assistant's log says why.
